summary: Independent review of the existing complete catalogue-screen packet: all 33 directed links are retained (27 explicit, 6 inferred), all outgoing from AdicSpaces, and all eight overlaps are retained (seven rescope, one keep). The review corrects coherent-cohomology closure, the scope of perfectoid closed immersions, the adic categorical quotient relation, the early A_inf/Witt topology boundary and the general gluing evidence for weight space. Seven focal layers were spot-checked for omitted connections; no additional direct edge was justified. The 218 examination records (focal roadmap, 211 other atlas roadmaps and six new roadmaps) preserve the original screen with its provenance; they are not a claim that this reviewer repeated that whole screen. No mathematical source document or implementation status is changed.

overlaps.detail: Layer 5 (§5.1) defines open immersions and open adic subspaces. It defines closed immersions affinoid-locally by quotient pairs A/J with J closed and A/J sheafy, and proves independence of the chosen affinoid cover. R0 again constructs open and closed immersions (with separatedness and finite, smooth and étale maps) from local presentations. It also keeps closed analytic subspaces together with their coherent ideals.
overlaps.proposal: R0 imports Layer 5's open and closed immersions. In the locally strongly noetherian analytic category it adds the comparison between a closed analytic subspace with its coherent ideal sheaf and a Layer 5 closed immersion; the required strongly noetherian quotient hypotheses are checked before applying Layer 4. Separated, finite, smooth and étale maps, completed tensor products, fibre products, diagonals and coherent-ideal refinements stay in R0. Nothing that needs fibre products moves into AdicSpaces.

overlaps.detail: Layer 5 defines morphisms of affinoid adic spaces topologically of finite type via quotient mappings from weighted restricted power-series algebras, and morphisms locally of finite type, with rational-localisation and refinement compatibility (§5.2). It also constructs closed discs and polydiscs (§5.4). A2, whose canonical owner is PartII, again constructs analytic balls and locally finite-type morphisms.
overlaps.proposal: A2 and its PartII owner import Layer 5's locally finite-type morphisms and prove the comparison with the selected Huber definition in the noetherian analytic scope. They use the existing closed polydiscs as the base case and add relative balls over an affinoid pair. Tori, continuous Kähler differentials, the analytic Jacobian criterion, smoothness, diagonals, separated/proper/partially proper maps, analytification and formal models remain downstream.

overlaps.detail: The overlap is limited to open immersions and comparison with quotient-defined closed subspaces. Layer 5 uses a closed ideal J, a sheafy quotient pair and the required plus-ring data. ECD Definition 5.6 instead defines a general closed immersion of perfectoid spaces by the injection and underlying closed-immersion conditions. Definition 5.7 separately singles out Zariski and strongly Zariski closed immersions; a surjective affinoid quotient with the prescribed integral-closure plus ring is the strongly Zariski case, not the definition of every closed immersion. P4 deliberately retains these distinctions.
overlaps.proposal: Reuse Layer 5 open immersions. Prove a comparison for its quotient-defined closed subspaces when the quotient pair is perfectoid, including quotient topology and the integral-closure plus-ring identification. Do not replace the general ECD 5.6 closed-immersion carrier by this quotient case. Keep ECD 5.6, 5.7, diagonal/separatedness and valuative criteria in P4. Keep the reverse Zariski-to-strongly-Zariski result as the Q4 return using BS22 7.4/7.5; it is not an elementary consequence of Layer 5 and must not be removed as duplication.

overlaps.detail: Layer 6 (§6.4) supplies the wandering-window local isomorphisms: the disjoint orbit decomposition of the inverse image of q(W), the homeomorphism W -> q(W), and the natural topological-ring, plus-ring and residue-valuation comparisons that make the chart map an isomorphism in 𝒱. Section 6.2 supplies Frobenius scaling of κ. These inputs do not themselves construct a categorical fibre product Y ×_X Y; fibre products are outside the upstream scope. F2 requires that categorical relation before its diamond-level quotient comparison.
overlaps.proposal: Import the existing local isomorphisms, orbit decomposition and radius normalisation through F0. Retain in F2 the construction and proof that the adic categorical relation is the disjoint union of Frobenius graphs, using the required fibre-product/morphism interfaces; do not call this only a set-theoretic identification. Retain its compatible diamondification, equivariance, effectiveness, quotient-sheaf covering and β_F with independence of pseudouniformiser and windows. Thus only repeated wandering-chart proofs are removed; the adic relation and all new diamond descent statements remain.

overlaps.detail: Layer 6 constructs the absolute adic quotient for E = Q_p over a perfect complete rank-one characteristic-p field. RF1 constructs the relative quotient for general E and perfectoid bases, with gluing, descent and compatibility of sheaves and valuations. RF0:annuli's fixed-field ring comparison and a later diamond comparison do not on their own state the adic-level quotient comparison.
overlaps.proposal: Keep both scopes. Require an adic-space isomorphism in the specialisation E = Q_p, S = Spa(F, O_F), extending the RF0:annuli ring identification and compatible with Frobenius, wandering windows and quotient maps. The fixed-field diamond comparison should be induced by that isomorphism. A (p,mu)- versus (p,[varpi])-adic comparison must state that mu reduces to a nonzero topologically nilpotent element of O_F and prove cofinality of the defining ideals.
